chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskan, from one whom he mentioned, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
Regarding the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
“So what has made them patient upon the Fire?”
So he عليه السلام said: “How patient they are in doing that which they know will cause them to end up in the Fire.”

key_terms.أَصْبَرَهُمْ: How patient they are; expressing astonishment at their endurance in sinful conduct
key_terms.اللَّهِ: Allah, the Exalted, whose statement is being explained
key_terms.النَّارِ: The Fire; hellfire as the outcome of their deeds
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; an honorific for Allah
key_terms.يَعْلَمُونَ: They know; indicating conscious awareness of the consequence
key_terms.يُصَيِّرُهُمْ: It causes them to end up; leads them toward a final outcome

ai.seo_question: What does “فَمَا أَصْبَرَهُمْ عَلَى النَّارِ” mean in Shia tafsir?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse as expressing amazement at people who persist in deeds they know will lead them to hellfire. Its significance lies in highlighting moral stubbornness and conscious disobedience as a grave spiritual danger.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Usman Bin Isa, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from the one who mentioned it,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[2:175] so what is their patience upon the Fire.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What caused them to be patient upon a deed what they knew was going to take them to the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from those he has mentioned (in his book) from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“About the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy,
‘What has made them remain so patient in the fire?’ [2:175]
The Imam said, ‘What has made them so patiently do something that they know will lead them to the fire?”’
